{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Spring Security 6 with Java 17 and Spring Boot-compatible configuration, exposing security as an opt-in application configuration.",
    "Implement file-based authentication using an external properties or YAML file containing users, password hashes, and roles; do not store passwords in source code.",
    "Implement LDAP authentication through Spring Security LDAP, with configurable URL, base DN, manager credentials, user search, group search, and role mapping.",
    "Apply authorization at the endpoint request-mapping layer using Admin and Viewer roles, with a configurable default-deny policy for unspecified endpoints.",
    "Implement the Kerberized HDFS sink using Hadoop security APIs and UserGroupInformation, supporting keytab and principal configuration while avoiding credentials in application source code.",
    "Treat the mass-ingestion requirement as a time-boxed discovery and design spike only; produce an integration-options comparison and a recommended design rather than production implementation.",
    "Implement the HBase sink using the standard HBase client API with configurable connection, table, column-family, row-key, and mutation mapping settings.",
    "Implement the File Roll sink as an append-oriented local filesystem sink with configurable directory, filename pattern, rollover size or time threshold, and flush behavior.",
    "Implement the JMX source using Spring Integration JMX support and expose configurable notification subscription and event mapping behavior.",
    "Use a common configuration and lifecycle pattern for all modules, with validation of required properties at startup and clear operational error messages.",
    "Use unit tests with mocks for normal logic and integration tests with embedded, containerized, or test-double external services where a real Hadoop, LDAP, HBase, or JMX environment is not available."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is added to an existing Java/Spring codebase with a functional build, test framework, endpoint registry, and established coding conventions.",
    "The target runtime is Java 17 or newer and the build uses Maven or an equivalent dependency-management system.",
    "The existing application exposes multiple endpoints on port 9393, and the endpoint inventory and authorization integration points can be determined during implementation.",
    "File-based security means application-managed users and roles loaded from an external file; operating-system file permissions and enterprise identity federation are out of scope.",
    "LDAP server availability, directory schema, certificates, and production credentials will be supplied by the deployment environment; implementation uses configurable schema mappings.",
    "Admin has full access and Viewer has read-oriented access; exact endpoint-specific exceptions will be finalized from the existing endpoint behavior.",
    "Kerberos infrastructure, Hadoop libraries, HDFS, and keytabs are available for deployment and environment-level validation; no Hadoop cluster administration is included.",
    "The HDFS sink must preserve the existing sink contract and add Kerberos authentication without redesigning unrelated data pipelines.",
    "The mass-ingestion spike covers investigation, design collaboration, decision records, and documentation only, as explicitly stated by the spike scope.",
    "The HBase sink targets a compatible HBase client version and does not include HBase cluster provisioning, schema administration, or performance tuning for a production-scale cluster.",
    "File Roll sink rollover means creating a new local file based on configurable size and/or time criteria; distributed filesystems and cross-process locking are out of scope.",
    "The JMX source consumes JMX notifications from configured MBeans and converts them into the application's existing event/message format.",
    "Security, sink, and source modules require configuration documentation and representative automated tests, but not a complete production operations manual.",
    "Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, integration verification, and developer documentation; it excludes elapsed waiting time for external teams and production deployment."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Baseline analysis and endpoint inventory",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing project structure, build, endpoint implementations, module conventions, configuration model, extension points, and current test coverage; identify all endpoints that must be protected.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Increment architecture and configuration design",
      "activity_description": "Define module boundaries, common configuration conventions, activation and precedence rules for file and LDAP security, role semantics, external-client lifecycle, error handling, and compatibility with the existing application.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "File-based security implementation",
      "activity_description": "Add external file loading, password-hash handling, user and role mapping, configuration validation, authentication provider wiring, and opt-in activation for file-based security.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "LDAP security implementation",
      "activity_description": "Add configurable LDAP context, bind or manager authentication, user and group searches, role mapping, connection settings, TLS-related configuration hooks, and opt-in LDAP authentication.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Endpoint role-based access control",
      "activity_description": "Apply Admin and Viewer authorization rules to the complete endpoint inventory, implement default access behavior for unspecified endpoints, and ensure unauthenticated and unauthorized responses are consistent.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Security automated tests and configuration documentation",
      "activity_description": "Add tests for file authentication, LDAP authentication using test doubles, role authorization, default-deny behavior, configuration errors, and representative secured endpoint requests; document setup examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Kerberized HDFS sink implementation",
      "activity_description": "Extend or create the HDFS sink to authenticate with Kerberos using principal and keytab or equivalent Hadoop configuration, establish the secured filesystem client, write records, and handle authentication and filesystem failures.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Kerberized HDFS sink validation",
      "activity_description": "Add unit and integration-oriented tests for credential configuration, login behavior, write success, retry or failure handling, resource cleanup, and compatibility with the existing non-Kerberized sink behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Mass-ingestion integration spike and design specification",
      "activity_description": "Investigate non-JDBC-dependent database ingestion options, compare drivers, change-data-capture, bulk-export, and connector approaches, collaborate on trade-offs, recommend an approach, and document the resulting design and open risks.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "HBase sink implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable HBase connectivity and lifecycle management, row-key and column-family mapping, put or mutation generation, batching behavior, error handling, and integration with the existing sink interface.",
      "most_likely_effort": 52
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "HBase sink tests and examples",
      "activity_description": "Test row and column mapping, batch writes, connection failures, resource cleanup, configuration validation, and representative HBase interactions using mocks or a test HBase environment; add configuration examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "File Roll sink implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement local filesystem event writing, configurable file naming, append and flush behavior, time- or size-based rollover, directory creation, restart handling, and write-failure reporting.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "File Roll sink tests",
      "activity_description": "Test event serialization, file creation, rollover boundaries, restart behavior, filesystem errors, concurrent lifecycle operations, and configuration validation using temporary directories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A14",
      "activity_name": "JMX source implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement JMX connection and MBean notification subscription, configurable object-name and notification filtering, event conversion, reconnect or shutdown handling, and integration with the application source lifecycle.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A15",
      "activity_name": "JMX source tests and documentation",
      "activity_description": "Test notification subscription, filtering, event mapping, connection failures, cleanup, and configuration behavior with a test MBean or local JMX server; document usage and examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A16",
      "activity_name": "Cross-module configuration, dependency, and operational documentation",
      "activity_description": "Integrate dependencies and configuration metadata, add sample configurations for all modules, document mutual exclusivity or precedence rules, startup validation, security setup, and operational troubleshooting.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A17",
      "activity_name": "End-to-end integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Exercise representative secured endpoints and source-to-sink flows, verify module coexistence and backward compatibility, test configuration permutations, and resolve integration defects found during the complete increment validation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A18",
      "activity_name": "Build, quality checks, and release readiness",
      "activity_description": "Run formatting, static analysis, dependency checks, full automated test suites, packaging, reproducibility checks, changelog or release notes, and final implementation cleanup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 504
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Security 6 with Java 17 and Spring Boot-compatible configuration, exposing security as an opt-in application configuration.
Implement file-based authentication using an external properties or YAML file containing users, password hashes, and roles; do not store passwords in source code.
Implement LDAP authentication through Spring Security LDAP, with configurable URL, base DN, manager credentials, user search, group search, and role mapping.
Apply authorization at the endpoint request-mapping layer using Admin and Viewer roles, with a configurable default-deny policy for unspecified endpoints.
Implement the Kerberized HDFS sink using Hadoop security APIs and UserGroupInformation, supporting keytab and principal configuration while avoiding credentials in application source code.
Treat the mass-ingestion requirement as a time-boxed discovery and design spike only; produce an integration-options comparison and a recommended design rather than production implementation.
Implement the HBase sink using the standard HBase client API with configurable connection, table, column-family, row-key, and mutation mapping settings.
Implement the File Roll sink as an append-oriented local filesystem sink with configurable directory, filename pattern, rollover size or time threshold, and flush behavior.
Implement the JMX source using Spring Integration JMX support and expose configurable notification subscription and event mapping behavior.
Use a common configuration and lifecycle pattern for all modules, with validation of required properties at startup and clear operational error messages.
Use unit tests with mocks for normal logic and integration tests with embedded, containerized, or test-double external services where a real Hadoop, LDAP, HBase, or JMX environment is not available.
assumptions: The increment is added to an existing Java/Spring codebase with a functional build, test framework, endpoint registry, and established coding conventions.
The target runtime is Java 17 or newer and the build uses Maven or an equivalent dependency-management system.
The existing application exposes multiple endpoints on port 9393, and the endpoint inventory and authorization integration points can be determined during implementation.
File-based security means application-managed users and roles loaded from an external file; operating-system file permissions and enterprise identity federation are out of scope.
LDAP server availability, directory schema, certificates, and production credentials will be supplied by the deployment environment; implementation uses configurable schema mappings.
Admin has full access and Viewer has read-oriented access; exact endpoint-specific exceptions will be finalized from the existing endpoint behavior.
Kerberos infrastructure, Hadoop libraries, HDFS, and keytabs are available for deployment and environment-level validation; no Hadoop cluster administration is included.
The HDFS sink must preserve the existing sink contract and add Kerberos authentication without redesigning unrelated data pipelines.
The mass-ingestion spike covers investigation, design collaboration, decision records, and documentation only, as explicitly stated by the spike scope.
The HBase sink targets a compatible HBase client version and does not include HBase cluster provisioning, schema administration, or performance tuning for a production-scale cluster.
File Roll sink rollover means creating a new local file based on configurable size and/or time criteria; distributed filesystems and cross-process locking are out of scope.
The JMX source consumes JMX notifications from configured MBeans and converts them into the application's existing event/message format.
Security, sink, and source modules require configuration documentation and representative automated tests, but not a complete production operations manual.

Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, integration verification, and developer documentation; it excludes elapsed waiting time for external teams and production deployment.
